messages:
rachel_cs: Heads-up: NovaApps onboarding blocked in staging. Their serverless backend using our Node server SDK gets intermittent 401s and a trailing set of 429s when the worker pool ramps. They just moved to server SDK v2.0.0-beta and are using tenant-level routing via `X-Redwood-Tenant`.

 tom_eng: can you paste the server logs they sent? and which token flow are they using (service token vs ephemeral)?

 rachel_cs: They sent this snippet from their lambda logs: `401 Unauthorized - missing_tenant_header` followed by `429 Too Many Requests` when retries kick in. Token type: service token tied to acct `acct_nova`.

 jia_se: interesting. missing_tenant_header suggests requests are hitting the multi-tenant router that expects the header for per-tenant routing. If the SDK dropped the header for some POST/stream paths, that could cause the router to reject with 401. The 429s then look like client retry fanout before the app noticed persistent 4xx.

 tom_eng: @rachel_cs can NovaApps share the raw request capture (headers) for one failed request? also their SDK config (any custom middleware)?

 rachel_cs: asked and they pasted: ```
POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
Content-Type: application/json
// note: NO X-Redwood-Tenant header on this failed request
```

 rachel_cs: they added that their app uses a fix-up middleware that attaches tenant header only for some routes and it was missing on streaming endpoints.

 jia_se: ok that explains 401s. For the 429s: I see in our edge logs a rapid spike from their service IP when the warm-up script retried the failed connections. Our edge rate limiter (we recently reduced tolerance on stream handshake retries) returned 429 on subsequent attempts.

 tim_ops: infra note: we lowered stream_handshake_burst to 6s across us-east-1 last week to protect the runtime. That makes quick retry loops more likely to hit 429. I can temporarily increase the window for acct_nova or add a short trial exemption.

 tom_eng: mitigation steps for customer: 1) ensure X-Redwood-Tenant gets attached to every outbound request (including stream handshakes) 2) add exponential backoff / jitter on retries 3) if they need an immediate unblock, we can relax the rate window for 24-48h. Also pushing a patch in the SDK to ensure header propagation on streaming paths.

 rachel_cs: shared the SDK workaround: they patched middleware to always attach header and will redeploy. I told them to run a single controlled warmup with a 2s delay between connections.

 jia_se: for our side, I'll add a small safety: if a request is missing tenant header but has a valid service token mapping to a tenant, we should prefer token -> tenant mapping and return a clearer error. Filing an infra ticket.

 tim_ops: temporary change applied: increased stream_handshake_burst to 20s for acct_nova. Will auto-revert in 48h. Logged as policy-change #POL-2026-998.

 rachel_cs: NovaApps redeployed with header fix and warmup pacing. They retried and got no more 401s or 429s. Onboarding resumed.

 jia_se: follow-ups: 1) SDK team to include a note in v2 release notes about header propagation for streams 2) CS to add a one-liner to onboarding checklist: "server SDKs must set X-Redwood-Tenant on streams" 3) infra to add clearer 401 messaging when header missing but token present.

 tom_eng: marking this as low renewal risk now but note that auth friction during server integration can escalate. Thanks everyone.

 ratebot: Policy change applied for acct_nova by tim_ops at 2026-05-12T11:40:00Z.
